# Architecture Framework

**Purpose:** Auto-generate the architecture model (UML / C4 diagrams) from the live Go source. Static map of the workspace; consumed by memQL Cockpit's Topology drill-down navigator and by anything else that wants to talk about the system in software-engineering terms.

**Language:** Go (stdlib + `golang.org/x/tools`, no third-party renderers)

**Companion runtime:** `component/observe/` -- the per-invocation capture layer keyed by the same FQNs this framework produces.

**Embed point:** `embedded/topology.model.json` is generated by `cmd/memql-arch` and shipped baked into every binary that imports `component/architecture/embedded`.

---

## Why this exists

memQL Cockpit's Topology pane needs to show the user "what's in this system" at every level of zoom -- cluster, service, package, type, method. Hand-maintained diagrams drift; commercial diagram tools couple us to a renderer. The team-Go-team toolchain (`go/ast`, `go/types`, `golang.org/x/tools/go/packages`, `.../callgraph`) can give us everything we need from the source alone. This package is that pipeline: source -> typed graph -> on-disk JSON -> embedded asset -> cockpit drill-down.

The framework is intentionally **build-time**, not runtime. The model is a property of a commit, not of a running process. That matches what users expect when they look at a diagram ("this is the code as it is now") and gives the model the same versioning guarantee as any other source file.

---

## Directory layout

```
component/architecture/
├── CLAUDE.md              # This file
├── model/                 # The intermediate representation
│   ├── model.go             - Node, Edge, Kind, EdgeKind, Model
│   ├── ids.go               - Canonical fully-qualified ID format
│   ├── json.go              - On-disk format + schema versioning
│   └── index.go             - Derived lookup layer (children, in/out edges)
├── extract/               # Source -> IR pipeline
│   ├── extract.go           - Run(Options) -> *model.Model, the public entry
│   ├── workspace.go         - go.work / go.mod discovery
│   ├── archyaml.go          - Per-module arch.yaml schema + loader
│   ├── gomod.go             - readModulePath
│   ├── packages.go          - L2 (services) + L3 (packages, imports)
│   ├── types.go             - L4 (structs, interfaces, methods, fields, embeds, implements)
│   ├── observe_markers.go   - //memql:observe source-marker parser
│   ├── callgraph.go         - CHA call graph (EdgeCalls)
│   ├── cluster.go           - Synthetic L1 cluster root
│   └── util.go              - filepath helpers
└── embedded/              # Build-time //go:embed of the produced model.json
    ├── embedded.go          - Load() *model.Model, //go:generate directive
    └── topology.model.json  - Generated; checked in
```

---

## Diagrams supported

C4 + UML, mapped 1:1 onto Kind / EdgeKind in `model/model.go`:

| Diagram | Reads from the model |
|---|---|
| **System context (C4-L1)** | `KindCluster` + its `EdgeContains` services + (forthcoming) `EdgeRunsOn` deployment edges |
| **Container (C4-L2)** | `KindService` + `EdgeDependsOn` |
| **Package / dependency graph (C4-L3)** | `KindPackage` + `EdgeImports` (within a service) |
| **Class diagram (C4-L4)** | `KindType` + `KindInterface` + `EdgeHasField`, `EdgeEmbeds`, `EdgeImplements`, `EdgeContains` (method children) |
| **Sequence diagram** | Walk forward from an entrypoint over `EdgeCalls` |
| **Call graph / dependency graph** | `EdgeCalls` directly |
| **Activity diagram / flowchart (CFG)** | (Planned) `golang.org/x/tools/go/cfg` per-function |
| **State diagram** | (Planned) annotation-driven, via doc-comment hints |
| **ERD** | (Planned) parse the `.memql` concept tree |
| **Deployment diagram** | (Planned) `deploy/k8s/` manifests + `scripts/deploy/` |

The model is **renderer-agnostic** -- exporters (PlantUML, D2, Mermaid) can write a model -> text translation any time, but the production consumer (cockpit) renders directly from the Go model into the tcell canvas.

---

## ID format

Every entity gets a stable, format-deterministic ID (`model.ID`). The format is documented in `model/model.go` and the constructors in `model/ids.go` are the single source for assembling them. The format matters because the same string is the join key used by:

- The cockpit's drill-down (which Node is selected)
- `component/observe`'s per-FQN level cache (which method to capture at what verbosity)
- The `code_invocation` hypertable's `code_reference` column (which method produced this row)
- The `v1:observability:codeProfile` concept's `codeReference` field (live config override)
- The `v1:cluster:nodeType` concept's `codeReference` field (cluster node <-> code service link)

If you need to construct an ID from outside the model package, call the constructors; never inline the format string.

---

## Per-module `arch.yaml`

Each module's root may carry an `arch.yaml` declaring its service identity, descriptions, and explicit cross-service edges that the import graph can't see (gRPC peers, queue handoffs, etc.). Schema lives in `extract/archyaml.go`; a missing file is fine -- the loader defaults to the directory base name and `./...` roots.

memql, the product carrier repo, and memql-cockpit each have one at their root. Editing them is the canonical way to change the cockpit's L1/L2 labels and to declare deployment/runtime edges.

---

## The runtime side: `component/observe`

The architecture framework gives you the static map; `component/observe` is the runtime layer that emits per-invocation data keyed by the same FQNs. The two were designed together -- if you change the ID format here, the per-FQN cache in observe and the join queries the cockpit issues all need to move with you. See `component/observe/CLAUDE.md` for the runtime story.

---

## How to use

### Regenerate the model after code changes

```bash
make arch-model
```

**This is the only supported way** (memql#2844). The flag set is load-bearing
and lives in exactly one place, the `arch-model` target:

- `--calls` is NOT a default, and the artifact contains the call graph --
  121k edges with it, 21k without. Regenerating without it silently drops
  100k edges.
- `--reproducible` blanks `generated_at` and the absolute workspace path, and
  `--cluster memql` pins the cluster node's name, which otherwise comes from
  your checkout's FOLDER name. Without these the output differs on every run
  and on every machine, and `TestArchitectureModelIsCurrent` fails for
  everyone but you.

`go generate` in `embedded/` now shells out to this target, so the two cannot
disagree. Regenerating by hand is not supported; there is no shorter form that
produces the committed artifact.

Wall time is ~6s on the full workspace. Regenerate it LAST in any change that
touches Go, since the model describes the code. (Test-only changes need no
regeneration -- all three extractor passes set `Tests: false`.)

**A Go toolchain bump also invalidates it.** The model encodes stdlib-derived
facts -- promoted methods from embedded stdlib types, `implements` edges against
stdlib interfaces, signatures rendered with stdlib type names -- so a minor or
patch bump can move them. CI pins `go-version`, so this bites exactly on the PR
that raises it: regenerate there.

`make arch-model-check` (or plain `go test ./...`) verifies the committed model
matches the code.

The artifact is written **compact, on one line**. Pretty-printing it produced a
1.26M-line file whose one-time reorder GitHub could not diff at all -- the API
returned *"this diff is taking too long to generate"*, which fails the `changes`
job and blocks the PR. So do not read it as a diff; the gate above is what
tells you whether it is right.

### Consume the model from another component

```go
import (
    "github.com/znasllc-io/memql/component/architecture/embedded"
    "github.com/znasllc-io/memql/component/architecture/model"
)

m, err := embedded.Load()
if err != nil { ... }
ix := model.NewIndex(m)

// L1 -> L2 enumeration
for _, root := range ix.Roots() {
    for _, svc := range ix.Children(root.ID) {
        // ...
    }
}
```

### Annotate a function for observability

```go
//memql:observe verbose redact=password
func (h *Handler) Login(ctx context.Context, user, password string) (err error) {
    ...
}
```

The extractor stamps `observe_level: "verbose"` and `redact_args: "password"` onto the Method node's Attrs; the cockpit's drill-down shows the badge, and the observe runtime honors the redact list.

---

## What's deliberately out of scope here

- **Rendering.** The model is the IR. Cockpit's `cli/cluster/architecture.go` is one renderer; future exporters (PlantUML, D2, Mermaid) live elsewhere.
- **Runtime instrumentation.** That's `component/observe`. The bridge is the ID format.
- **DSL concepts and SQL migrations.** The model is pure Go; concepts and hypertable schemas for the observability side live in `dsl/observability/` and `component/database/memory-nodes/migrations/`.
